access.rpcHelp:
RPC is how applications talk to a node: reading blocks and balances and sending transactions all go through it. Methods are grouped by purpose and written as group:method, such as eth:call; group:* means the whole group.

Common groups: eth reads chain data and sends transactions; net is network status; txpool is the transaction pool; admin manages the node (peers, log level); qbft is consensus and validator voting.

Most applications only need eth and net. admin and qbft can change the node or cast votes, so give them only to identities that really need them.
access.docPrivateApi: Besu docs: QBFT and PERM methods
access.subtitleAllowlist: Nodes only accept transactions sent from blockchain addresses on the allowlist (the setting applies to our nodes only and cannot affect other nodes)

behind.text: Besu reports how far it trails the head.

catching.text: Besu reports it is still syncing.

detail.ownExpectedHelp: The last {{window}} blocks were produced in turn by {{v}} validators; this is each one’s even share. Under 70% of it counts as "Low".
detail.ownMissedHelp: Of its turns in this window, how many it missed and the next validator took over.
detail.turnTimeHelp: When it produced this block, written into the block when it proposed. A missed turn has no block of its own, so it stays empty.
detail.ownWindow: Block production over the last {{window}} blocks

turnRule.intro: Each row is one of its turns to propose.

ontime.text: It sent its block before the round timeout.

missed.text: Nothing was produced before the timeout, so the next validator produced this height. That is why the row has no block time.

detail.turnGasHelp:
Gas this block actually used, followed by its share of the block's limit (gasLimit).

A validator can set a target (target-gas-limit) that the blocks it proposes move toward, so blocks from different validators can have different limits. Close to 100% means the block was full and other transactions wait for the next one.
detail.jvmHeapHelp:
Besu is a Java program with its own memory limit set at start-up (the heap limit). This chart shows how much of that limit is used, which is not the same as host memory: the host can look fine while Besu's own limit is nearly full.

When it is, Besu keeps pausing to clean up memory, blocks get slow, and when it is full Besu crashes.

The dashed line marks usage {{th}}, the same number as the alert rule.
detail.diskCardHelp:
Left: how much of the disk is used; {{th}} shows "High", the same threshold as the alert rule.

Right: days until full at the growth rate of the last 7 days; "Over a year" when not growing or longer; "Not enough data" with less than 7 days of data. Under {{days}} days shows "Filling up"; plan to expand.

validators.histResultHelp:
Passed: a majority voted and the validator set changed; it ended at the block where that took effect.

Not passed: no majority by the epoch change, so the on-chain tally was cleared and it ended at the epoch block; or every organization withdrew its votes and the count dropped to zero, ending at the block where the last vote was cancelled. Nodes that still hold the vote cast it again in the new epoch, which shows as a new record.

Withdrawing only affects your organization's votes: once withdrawn they no longer count, and other organizations' votes are untouched.

summary.PlatformDown: Platform down; no node metrics can be collected
summary.NodeTxpoolStale: Node {{node}}: pool transactions waiting long ({{value}} s)

cause.PlatformDown: Prometheus cannot read the platform's metrics. Node metrics are collected through the platform, so while it is down no node can be read and node-offline alerts are held back. Fix the platform first.
cause.NodeOffline: Prometheus cannot read metrics from {{node}}: the agent is not connected to the platform, or it has stopped.
cause.BesuMetricsDown: The agent is reachable, but Besu's metrics are not: Besu is not running, or metrics are not enabled.
cause.NodePeerCountLow: Too few P2P connections; the node risks being isolated.
cause.NodeCpuHigh: The CPU has been maxed out for a while; block production and sync may slow down.
cause.NodeMemHigh: Host memory is tight; Besu may slow down or be stopped by the system.
cause.NodeDiskHigh: Chain data keeps growing; plan to add disk space early.
cause.NodeBehind: This node cannot keep up with the chain head, possibly because sync is slow or it has too few peers. If its peers look fine but it stays behind, restart Besu.
cause.NodeJvmHeapHigh: A nearly full Java heap causes frequent GC and slower block production, and eventually an out-of-memory stop; consider raising Besu's -Xmx.
cause.NodeTxpoolFull: Once the pool is full, new transactions are rejected. Check the transaction pool tab for stuck transactions (nonce gaps, gas too low), or raise tx-pool-max-size.
cause.NodeTxpoolStale: Usually a nonce gap or gas price too low; check the transaction pool tab for which account.
cause.ChainSlow: The time since the last block exceeds the set multiple of the normal block time. Common causes: a validator is not producing (each time it is its turn, the chain waits for a timeout before moving on), heavy node load, or network latency.
cause.ChainSlowSevere: A validator may be offline, or validators may have lost consensus.
cause.ValidatorsMissing: Some validators are not producing blocks, but the chain keeps going; a few more and it will stop. See Chain health for which ones.
cause.QuorumLost: More validators are not producing than the fault tolerance allows, so the chain cannot reach the threshold and has stopped producing blocks.

chain.title: Chain health
chain.trendsTitle: Block time and throughput over time
chain.empty: No other nodes visible yet. Once a node is registered and connected, the nodes it sees are listed here.

dotHelp.err: Red (critical): one of your nodes has its agent offline or its RPC unreachable; or, while consensus is stalled, a validator that cannot be reached.
dotHelp.warn: Orange (attention): a validator not in consensus while the chain still produces blocks, or blocks behind {{lag}}. The threshold can be changed in alert settings.
dotHelp.stalled: While consensus is stalled, who is taking part cannot be seen; only unreachable validators are marked.
dotHelp.idle: It missed its proposer turn twice in a row.

who.text: Validators are recorded on-chain, so all of them appear. Regular nodes appear only when one of your nodes is connected to them.

behind.text: How many blocks it trails the chain head.

lastProposed.text: The last block it produced as proposer.

missed.text: Times in the last 1000 blocks it was due to propose but timed out and the next validator took over.

nodesHelp.source: Data in this table for nodes outside your organization all comes from the blockchain. The actual state of other organizations' machines (CPU, disk, sync) needs cross-org monitoring, an Enterprise feature.

enterprise.lead:
For one company or organization managing its own nodes, the open-source edition is enough.
When several companies or organizations need to run consortium governance and audit controls, we recommend upgrading to Enterprise.
enterprise.support: Includes deployment, feature customization and upgrade support.

addPeer.pasteHint: Press Enter to add it to the list and paste the next one.
addPeer.candidatesHint: Peers your nodes are connected to that are not on the list.

addNode.subtitle: Install the agent on the host running Besu so the platform can monitor and manage the node through it
addNode.name: Note (optional)
addNode.nameHint: A note for yourselves, e.g. location or purpose; can be changed later.
addNode.nodeIdHelp:
A unique identifier you define for this platform, unrelated to the Besu node ID (enode public key).

It cannot change after joining and is used in certificates, URLs, metric labels and the audit log.

Format: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
addNode.nodeIdBad: Invalid: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, not starting with a hyphen
addNode.nodeIdFixed: Letters, digits and - only (stored lowercase, can't start with -); can't be changed after joining.
addNode.inboundHint: Address the agent uses to reach the platform. Override it behind NAT or VPN.
addNode.sourcesHint: Only an agent connecting from these IPs can use this join code. Leave empty for no restriction.
addNode.sourcesHelp:
Stops a leaked join code from being used on another machine.
Enter the node host's IP or range (e.g. 10.0.0.31, 10.0.0.0/24); several are fine, separated by commas or spaces.
Checked only when the node joins; the node changing its IP later is fine. Behind NAT, enter the NAT device's public IP.
addNode.sourcesBad: Invalid: IP or CIDR, separated by commas or spaces
addNode.nodeIdTaken: A node with this id already exists
addNode.offlineTtl: Offline installs usually take over an hour; 24 hours is recommended.
addNode.methodOnlineHint: The node host fetches install.sh and the agent from the platform (it needs to reach the platform's web address).
addNode.methodOfflineHint: Download the bundle here and copy it to the node host yourself. Use this when the host cannot reach the platform's web address, or files must be reviewed first.
addNode.noBundle: The platform has no agent binaries, so no bundle is available (AGENT_BINARY_DIR).
addNode.bundleContents: Contains install.sh, the upgrade script and agent {{version}} ({{arches}}); the matching architecture is picked at install time.
addNode.stepTransfer: Copy it to the node host
addNode.transferHint: Use your usual file transfer (scp, an internal file server). The command verifies the checksum before unpacking.
addNode.verifyFirst: Verifies install.sh before running it as root; nothing is installed if the check fails.
addNode.confirmHint: Press Done to return to the node list; that row shows the join progress.
addNode.codeInCmd: Already in the command below; you can also copy it on its own. Shown once; you cannot view it again after leaving this page.
addNode.ttlAskBody: A new join code replaces this one, which stops working right away. Copy the command again if you already copied it.

nodeSet.quarantinedHint: Agent certificate verification failed; the platform stopped collecting data from this node.
nodeSet.portsHint: Must match Besu's rpc-http-port and metrics-port. This changes the ports the platform has on record; the platform cannot change Besu's own settings, so change those on the node.
nodeSet.lastRead: RPC is unreachable; showing the last values read.
nodeSet.logHint: Takes effect right away but only changes the running Besu; nothing is written to its config file, so after a restart Besu goes back to the level set there.

logLevelHelp.WARN: Adds warnings: something may be wrong, but Besu keeps running.
logLevelHelp.INFO: Besu's default. Adds routine messages such as imported blocks and peer connections.
logLevelHelp.DEBUG: Adds detail for troubleshooting; noticeably more output.
logLevelHelp.TRACE: The most detail, down to each internal step; very large output.
logLevelHelp.note: Each level includes everything above it. After troubleshooting with DEBUG or TRACE, set it back to INFO.

what.text: A small program on the node's host; the bridge between the platform and this node.

use.text: The status, charts and logs you see on the platform, and actions such as pushing peers or applying the address allowlist, all go through it to Besu. The agent opens the connection to the platform and the platform never connects in, so the host needs no inbound port for the platform.

where.text: On the same host as Besu, as a systemd service or a Docker container (both named besu-agent). Settings are in /etc/besu-agent, the agent certificate in /var/lib/besu-agent.

nodeSet.upgradeOld: This node runs agent {{v}}; {{latest}} is available. Run the command below on this node's host.
nodeSet.upgradeLatest: This node already runs the latest agent ({{v}}); no upgrade needed.
nodeSet.upgradeRun: Run the command below on this node's host.

when.text: A platform update brings a newer agent, but agents already installed on nodes don't update themselves. Upgrade when the capability checklist's Agent version row says an upgrade is available.

how.text: Copy the command on this card and run it on this node's host (needs sudo). Nothing to prepare: the command uses this node's agent certificate to download the new version from the platform and checks its checksum. Works for both systemd and Docker installs.

effect.text: The agent restarts and is disconnected from the platform for a few seconds; Besu is not affected.

nodeSet.rejoinHint: Reinstalls the agent on the node's host with a new agent certificate so this node can reconnect to the platform.
nodeSet.rejoinHelp:
Use it after rebuilding the host, or when the agent certificate is no longer valid and the agent can't connect.
The node id and its history are kept; it does not become a new node. It also works while the agent on this host is connected; the command stops it first.
nodeSet.rejoinOnce: The join code is valid for 1 hour and shown only once.
nodeSet.deleteHint:
Revokes this node's agent certificates and unenrolls it: the agent disconnects right away, the platform stops monitoring and managing it, and this node's own settings on the platform (custom peers, addresses added just for it) are deleted. Besu on the node keeps running; block production and sync are not affected.

To remove the agent from the machine as well, run sudo /usr/local/sbin/bsos-uninstall on it.
nodeSet.deleteBody: Unenroll {{id}}? Its agent certificates are revoked and the agent disconnects at once; Besu on the node keeps running. Enrolling it again needs a new join code.
nodeSet.deleteType: Type the node id to confirm
nodeSet.besuHint: These are Besu startup settings. The platform cannot change them directly; following the steps below, edit them on the node and restart Besu.
nodeSet.nameHint: A note for yourselves, e.g. location or purpose.

allowlist.help:
The shared list applies to every node with "Use shared list" on; changes are pushed to all of them, with no restart.

Each node can also add its own addresses; a node with "Use shared list" off accepts only its own additions.

These nodes only accept transactions sent by listed addresses; blocks produced by other nodes are not re-checked.

Nodes without it enabled accept transactions from any address (as long as the sender can reach their RPC).
allowlist.emptyWarn: The shared list is empty: once applied, nodes accept only their own additions; a node with none refuses every transaction.
allowlist.holders: Nodes already have a list: {{nodes}}, {{count}} accounts combined.
allowlist.noneOn: None of your nodes has enabled authorized addresses yet, so they accept transactions from any address (as long as the sender can reach their RPC).
allowlist.notAppliedHint: The list is empty and refuses every transaction; press "Re-apply" to write the shared list
allowlist.emptyHint: The list is empty and refuses every transaction
allowlist.fileFilled: The command includes the {{count}} shared addresses, so the list takes effect after the restart without "Re-apply".
allowlist.fileFilledOwn: The command includes the {{count}} shared addresses and this node's {{own}} additions, so the list takes effect after the restart without "Re-apply".
allowlist.fileEmpty: The shared list is still empty: enabled like this, the node refuses every transaction. Add addresses to the shared list first, then copy the command.
allowlist.resultFailHint: For nodes not updated, open the node’s tab and press "Re-apply".
allowlist.newDesc: Addresses added here apply to this node only, on top of the shared list. They take effect when you press Apply.
allowlist.resyncBody: Writes the platform's list (shared list plus own additions) to {{node}} again.
allowlist.resyncBodyOwnOnly: Writes {{node}}'s own addresses to the node again.
allowlist.gapTitle: Differences from the node's actual list
allowlist.sharedOffTitle: Stop using the shared list on {{node}}?
allowlist.sharedOffBody: {{node}} will only accept its {{count}} own addresses, and later changes to the shared list will not reach it.
allowlist.sharedOffBodyNone: {{node}} will stop using the shared list, and later changes to it will not reach this node.
allowlist.sharedOffEmpty: This node has no own addresses yet: once off, its list is empty and it refuses every transaction.
allowlist.sharedOnTitle: Use the shared list on {{node}} again?
allowlist.sharedOnBody: {{node}} will apply the shared list ({{shared}} addresses) and keep its {{count}} own additions.
allowlist.applySkipNotShared: {{nodes}} do not use the shared list and are not affected.
allowlist.applyNone: No enabled node will apply this list right now.
allowlist.applySkipCustom: Addresses each node added for itself are kept.
allowlist.applySkipOff: {{nodes}} are not enabled or unreachable and will not be updated.
allowlist.csvDone: Imported {{n}} addresses from {{file}}, skipped {{skipped}} (duplicate or invalid). Press Apply to take effect.
allowlist.inShared: This address is already on the shared list, which every node applies.
allowlist.noExtra: Nothing added for this node yet.
allowlist.nodeOff: This node has not enabled authorized addresses, so it accepts transactions from any address (as long as the sender can reach its RPC).
allowlist.nodeOffFix: The enable setup guide writes the shared list into the allowlist file, so it takes effect after the restart; then it can have its own additions too.
allowlist.nodeUnreachable: This node is unreachable, so its list cannot be read or changed. Its state shows again once it is back.
allowlist.appliedWithOwn: Shared list and node allowlist applied
allowlist.csvHint: Import a CSV or text file: separate addresses with commas or new lines.

txpool.tooLarge: Pool too large to list · totals only
txpool.acctHelpPending: Transactions with consecutive nonces that can go into a block when their turn comes; the track's "Ready" below.
txpool.acctHelpQueued: A nonce before them is missing, so they wait until it arrives; the track's "Waiting" below.
txpool.trackHelp: A sender's transactions go on-chain one by one in nonce order. Green are the last few already on-chain; blue are in the pool and go in when their turn comes. If a nonce is missing (red dashed), everything after it waits (orange) until the sender resends the missing one.
txpool.helpHash: The transaction's unique ID (transaction hash), computed from its contents, so no two are the same. It's what the sending application gets back, and what you look the transaction up by once it's on-chain.
txpool.rsn_NONCE_TOO_FAR_IN_FUTURE_FOR_SENDER: Nonce too far ahead, earlier transactions missing
txpool.rsn_EXCEEDS_BLOCK_GAS_LIMIT: Needs more gas than a block allows
txpool.rsn_TX_SENDER_NOT_AUTHORIZED: Sender address not on the account allowlist
txpool.nodeNotFound: Node not found or not in this organization
txpool.off: Transaction pool not enabled (TXPOOL namespace, optional)
txpool.helpSize:
Transactions in the pool / pool limit.

Sometimes "Ready" plus "Waiting" is a few short of this total, because transactions just included in a block have not been cleared from the pool yet.

Usage {{pct}} shows "nearly full", the same threshold as the alert rule; when full, new transactions are refused.
txpool.helpPending: Transactions whose nonce is in sequence and can be included in the next block.
txpool.helpQueued: Transactions waiting for a missing earlier nonce. Above 0 means a sender is stuck; the list below shows which.
txpool.helpOldest: How long the oldest transaction in the pool has waited. {{sec}} seconds shows "long", the same threshold as the alert rule. Usually it is stuck behind an earlier nonce or the gas price is too low.
txpool.helpRejected:
Transactions this node’s pool refused in the last hour; reasons are listed below.

Every node checks incoming transactions, not only validators: a wrong nonce, too low a fee, a sender not on the allowlist or a full pool all lead to refusal.

On a node that serves RPC the sending application gets the error directly; a transaction relayed from another node is simply not kept or passed on.
txpool.accountsTitle: Senders with transactions waiting to go on-chain
txpool.helpMissing: Which nonces this sender is missing. Every transaction after a missing nonce has to wait; the sender must resend the missing one. The node cannot fill it in.
txpool.helpAge: For senders with a missing nonce: how long the first blocked transaction has waited. Otherwise: how long the oldest ready transaction has waited.
txpool.helpSource: "Local" transactions were sent straight to this node; "Relayed" came from other nodes. Senders with both show "Local + relayed".
txpool.footer: {{local}} sent to this node, {{relay}} relayed by other nodes, snapshot at {{at}}

extraPeers.ownHelp:
Pushed to this node only and reconnected if they drop; static-nodes.json and bootnodes are untouched.

With "Use shared list" on, this node connects to the shared list plus these; with it off, only to these.
extraPeers.ownEmpty: No peers added for this node yet.
extraPeers.sharedOffTitle: Stop using the shared list on {{node}}?
extraPeers.sharedOffBody:
The platform removes the shared-list peers it added to this node and keeps only its {{count}} own peers.

A peer listed only in this node’s static-nodes.json (and not the other way round) stays disconnected until Besu restarts.
extraPeers.sharedOffBodyNone:
The platform removes the shared-list peers it added to this node and adds no more; connections follow the node’s own static-nodes.json, bootnodes and discovery.

A peer listed only in this node’s static-nodes.json (and not the other way round) stays disconnected until Besu restarts.
extraPeers.sharedOnTitle: Use the shared list on {{node}} again?
extraPeers.sharedOnBody: This node also connects to the {{shared}} peers on the shared list and keeps its {{count}} own peers.
extraPeers.removeBody:
This node disconnects from “{{peer}}” within 30 seconds and stops dialling it; it may still connect again from its side or through discovery.

If it is also in this node’s static-nodes.json, it stays disconnected until Besu restarts.
extraPeers.sharedHelp:
One list for the whole organization. Every node with "Use shared list" on also connects to these peers and reconnects if they drop. Adding or removing a peer reaches every node with the switch on within 30 seconds; nothing needs applying.

Each node can add its own peers too; a node with the switch off connects only to its own.
extraPeers.offlineBody: This node is offline, so its connections cannot be read or changed; its state shows again once it is back.
extraPeers.idleBody: The platform does not connect this node to the shared-list peers; its own peers below still apply.
extraPeers.noAdminBody: This node's Besu does not expose the ADMIN RPC group (ADMIN is missing from rpc-http-api). The platform uses ADMIN calls to add peers and read who the node is connected to, so it cannot manage this node's peers yet.
extraPeers.noAdminFix: Follow the enable setup guide to add ADMIN to rpc-http-api, then restart Besu.
extraPeers.missingHelp:
The node keeps retrying on its own; if a Besu restart clears the list, the platform puts it back within 30 seconds. Nothing needs applying.

If it stays disconnected, the peer is usually offline, port 30303 is blocked, or the address is wrong.
extraPeers.sharedRemoveBody:
Every node with "Use shared list" on disconnects from “{{peer}}” within 30 seconds and stops dialling it; it may still connect again from its side or through discovery.

If one of those nodes also lists it in static-nodes.json, that node stays disconnected until Besu restarts.

cross-org.title: Cross-org node monitoring
cross-org.lead: Organizations grant each other access and see the whole consortium chain at a glance.

audit.title: Audit & reports
audit.lead: Who did what and when — complete, tamper-proof, and ready for auditors at any time.

node-keys.title: Node key management
node-keys.lead: Integrates with your existing key management infrastructure, bringing node keys under one managed home with traceable backup and rotation.

failover.title: Rapid failover
failover.lead: When a primary node fails, the standby takes over and service carries on.

incident.title: Incident response center
incident.lead: When an alert fires, best-practice steps guide the response; who handles it, how fast, and when it closes — all in view.

identity.title: Connect company accounts
identity.lead: Sign in with your institution's existing accounts; permissions follow your org groups.

maker-checker.title: Maker–checker
maker-checker.lead: One person prepares, another approves — built for internal control.

config-history.title: Settings change history
config-history.lead: Who changed which rule or channel and when, with before and after side by side.

custom-rules.title: Custom alert rules
custom-rules.lead: Write your own alert rules: metric, threshold, scope and duration are all yours to set.

rpc-node-scope.title: Per-node RPC access
rpc-node-scope.lead: Choose which nodes each RPC access identity can reach, so public services and internal systems stay apart.
rpc-node-scope.p1: Pick the nodes each identity can reach
rpc-node-scope.p2: Set it by node group, such as public or internal

consortium-sync.title: Consortium list sync
consortium-sync.lead: Compare shared lists with other members and apply them together once everyone approves.
